newsroom.definition: A room where journalists work together to prepare news stories.

editor-s-desk.definition: The editor’s work area for checking and organising articles before publication.

whiteboard.definition: A smooth board used for writing notes and planning ideas.

pinboard.definition: A board where papers and notices are attached with pins.

computer-terminal.definition: A computer station used to write, edit, or send news.

telephone.definition: A device used to speak with someone who is far away.

coffee-cup.definition: A small container used for drinking coffee or other drinks.

filing-cabinet.definition: A piece of furniture used to store documents in drawers.

notepad.definition: A small pad of paper used for writing quick notes.

wall-clock.definition: A clock fixed to a wall that shows the current time.

newspaper.definition: A printed or digital publication containing recent news and information.

headline.definition: A large title that introduces the main point of a news story.

article.definition: A piece of writing about a particular subject or event.

column.definition: A regular newspaper article written by the same writer.

photograph.definition: A picture made with a camera to record a person, place, or event.

caption.definition: Words placed beside a picture to explain what it shows.

classified-ad.definition: A small advertisement grouped with similar notices in a newspaper.

editorial.definition: An article that gives a publication’s opinion about an issue.

front-page.definition: The first page of a newspaper showing its most important stories.

back-page.definition: The last page of a newspaper, often with special features.

reporter.definition: A journalist who gathers information and writes news stories.

editor.definition: A person who checks, improves, and chooses written material.

photographer.definition: A person who takes photographs, especially for newspapers and news reports.

columnist.definition: A writer who regularly contributes a column to a publication.

cartoonist.definition: An artist who creates cartoons for newspapers, magazines, or online news.

proofreader.definition: A person who checks writing for spelling, grammar, and printing mistakes.

copy-editor.definition: An editor who improves the accuracy, clarity, and style of text.

correspondent.definition: A journalist who reports from a particular place or subject area.

intern.definition: A student or trainee working temporarily to gain experience.

publisher.definition: A person or company that produces and distributes publications.

press-pass.definition: An identity card allowing a journalist to enter an event.

notebook.definition: A book of blank pages for recording information and ideas.

pen.definition: A tool that uses ink to write on paper.

voice-recorder.definition: A device that records spoken sounds so a journalist can listen later.

camera.definition: A device that takes photographs or records video.

laptop.definition: A portable computer that folds shut like a book.

microphone.definition: A device that changes sound into an electrical recording or signal.

tripod.definition: A three-legged stand that keeps a camera steady.

press-release.definition: An official statement sent to journalists to announce news or an event.

interview-notes.definition: Written points that record what someone said during an interview.

draft.definition: An early version of writing that can still be changed.

deadline.definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.

layout.definition: The arrangement of text, pictures, and spaces on a page.

proof.definition: A test copy checked before a publication is printed.

printing-press.definition: A machine that produces many printed copies of a publication.

ink.definition: Coloured liquid or paste used for writing and printing.

paper-roll.definition: A long continuous sheet of paper wound around a tube.

folding-machine.definition: A machine that folds printed paper into the required shape.

delivery-truck.definition: A vehicle used to carry newspapers or goods to different places.

newsstand.definition: A small shop or stand that sells newspapers and magazines.

breaking-news.definition: Important news reported while an event is still happening or developing.

feature-story.definition: A longer article that explores a person, place, or topic.

opinion-piece.definition: An article in which a writer explains a personal view.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.

interview.definition: A conversation in which one person asks another questions.

investigation.definition: A careful search for facts about a serious or complex matter.

weather-report.definition: Information about current or expected weather conditions in a particular place.

sports-score.definition: The number of points or goals achieved in a sports game.

obituary.definition: A published notice about someone who has died.

advertisement.definition: A public message designed to promote a product or service.

classified.definition: An advertisement placed under a category with similar short notices.

cartoon.definition: A humorous drawing or comic strip, often about current events.

photo.definition: A picture captured with a camera for a record, report, or memory.

journalist.definition: A person who collects, checks, and reports news for the public.

printer.definition: A machine that produces paper copies of digital documents.

layout-designer.definition: A person who arranges text and images for publication pages.

source.definition: A person, document, or place that provides information.

publish.definition: To prepare and make writing available to the public.

print.definition: To produce words or images on paper using a machine.

distribute.definition: To deliver publications or information to many people in different places.

subscribe.definition: To pay regularly to receive a publication or service.

proofread.definition: To read writing carefully and correct errors before publication.

archive.definition: A collection of records kept for future reference.
